issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String, but the solution introduces a FeedResponse type and declares Animal.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. This cross-artifact return type mismatch contradicts the specification and will confuse students about the expected method signature and what to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change Animal.messageOnFeed() to return String and update all subclasses to return String (remove or avoid using FeedResponse), or alternatively update the problem statement and UML to specify FeedResponse as the return type. Prefer changing the solution to return String to preserve the described exercise design.

issues.description: Within the solution repository there is an inconsistency: Animal.messageOnFeed() is declared to return FeedResponse, but Goat.messageOnFeed() is implemented to return String. This internal mismatch makes the solution code non-compilable and contradicts the intended uniform method signature across subclasses.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across the solution: either change Goat.messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse (matching Animal) or change Animal.messageOnFeed() (and other subclasses) to return String. Prefer matching the problem statement by making all implementations return String.

issues.description: The problem specification and UML define Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (the animal sound) and describe farm methods (e.g., feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong) that print those String messages. The provided solution instead changes the method signature to public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed() and introduces a new FeedResponse class. This introduces a new type/identifier (FeedResponse) not mentioned in the problem/template, breaking the direct mapping between the required String-returning messageOnFeed() and the solution implementation. Students expecting to call messageOnFeed() to obtain a String (for printing in Farm or composing the song) will face confusion about the FeedResponse type and whether to use toString(), extract fields, or change method signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by making Animal.messageOnFeed() return String (as in the UML). Update Seal, Pig, and Goat implementations to return the required String messages (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). Remove or repurpose the FeedResponse class (or keep it but do not change the public messageOnFeed() signature) so the method signature and return type match the exercise description and template expectations.
